Fusagasugá is associated with the coffee farms around Bogotá. At Hacienda Coloma, visitors can follow coffee's journey from seeds and plants through harvesting to the finished cup. The plantation reveals a rural side of Colombia: behind a familiar drink lie cultivation, manual work and the processing of coffee beans.

The farm visit also includes an introduction to local rum. Tastings of a drink with coffee notes take place in the cellar, while regional cuisine continues the exploration of local products. Fusagasugá is a good destination for a dedicated introduction to coffee production during a stay in the capital.

### Galápagos Islands — a remarkable corner of Ecuador!

The Galápagos Islands are a picturesque, sunlit destination that captivates travelers with natural sights and pristine sandy beaches. Hot, sunny weather prevails for much of the year, offering ideal conditions for beach lovers and water activities.

The Galápagos Islands are also home to a remarkable range of endemic plant and animal life. Here visitors can swim with fur seals, encounter several species of penguins, dive alongside hammerhead sharks or watch giant tortoises weighing 200 kilograms. Located on the equator, approximately 600 miles west of Ecuador, the islands were discovered in 1535 by Tomás de Berlanga, the Spanish bishop of Panama, when his ship drifted past them. During the 17th and 18th centuries, pirates used the islands as meeting points and as places to obtain fresh food and water.

## Discovering endemic plants and wildlife

### When to visit the Galápagos Islands

The Galápagos Islands formally became part of Ecuador in 1832, and ten years later several small settlements had been established on some of the islands. After visiting the islands in 1835 and carrying out further studies of local wildlife, the English naturalist Charles Darwin noted that almost all the animals and plants here were endemic to the islands. This observation, of course, supported his famous theory of natural selection. The islands appeared on maps, and the wider world learned about the Galápagos. They became Ecuador's first national park and are now protected islands which, together with the surrounding marine reserve, have been designated World Heritage sites. The most interesting period for visiting the Galápagos Islands is considered to be December through May, when sea turtles lay their eggs and can be seen on virtually every island of the archipelago.

Gamboa lies where the Chagres River meets the Panama Canal. Forested riverbanks and water surround this nature-focused part of the route. From here, it is convenient to continue exploring the tropical ecosystems of the canal basin.

On the Panama City and Gamboa itinerary, travelers spend two nights at Gamboa Rainforest Resort. A separate day is devoted to Soberanía and the Panama Rainforest Discovery Center, followed by a boat trip on Gatun Lake and a visit to Monkey Island. Wildlife sightings depend on the animals' natural behavior.

In Gardner Bay on Española Island, the first thing to catch the eye is a bright ribbon of sand. Turquoise water laps gently at the shore, while sea lions rest nearby. One lies beside the surf, another lifts its head, and a third slowly returns to the ocean. You could spend a long time watching this beach scene.

The walk stays within the beach area; there is no trail leading inland from here. But the water's edge offers plenty of small discoveries. Española mockingbirds and other birds can be seen on shore, while snorkeling near the rocks offers glimpses of marine life. Whether visitors can enter the water depends on conditions in the bay.

After the rocky trail at Punta Suárez, Gardner Bay provides time for relaxed observation by the ocean. Stop, notice the changing shades of the water and give the animals room to move freely. The bay will especially appeal to travelers who want to combine a beautiful beach with a close encounter with Galápagos wildlife.
